items.title: Patient-directed discharge letter: a novel approach to improving patient knowledge and understanding of hospital-related events and adherence to discharge recommendations.
items.abstract: The transition from hospital to home poses significant challenges for patients, often due to inadequate understanding of hospital events and post-discharge plans. Standard discharge letters are typically directed to doctors rather than patients. To evaluate the effectiveness of a patient-directed discharge letter (PADDLE) in improving patient knowledge of their hospitalisation and post-discharge plans. A prospective randomised controlled trial was conducted across three centres in Sydney, Australia, involving patients hospitalised with one of 12 common cardiology, respiratory, general medical or endocrine conditions. A total of 163 participants (mean age 62.8 years, standard deviation 15.2; 31.3% female) were randomised 1:1 to receive either PADDLE plus a standard doctor-directed discharge letter (n = 79) or the standard discharge letter alone (n = 84). The primary outcome was participant knowledge of hospital information at 1 week after discharge. Secondary outcomes included understanding of hospital stay and adherence to discharge instructions. At 1 week post-discharge, participants receiving PADDLE demonstrated higher knowledge (mean difference 6.36 on a 0-100 scale; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.03, 11.68), greater understanding (mean difference 0.23 on a 1-5 scale; 95% CI 0.03, 0.49), and improved adherence (incidence rate ratio 1.27; 95% CI 1.05, 1.54). The intervention was highly valued, with 83% of participants reporting it as useful. PADDLE improved patient knowledge and understanding of discharge communication and adherence to post-discharge instructions. These findings support the use of structured, patient-centred discharge communication to enhance patient outcomes and continuity of care.

items.title: Digital Thoracic Drainage System-Derived Circuit Pressure and Air-Flow Changes in Relation to Echocardiographic Indices of Cardiac Function after Chest Tube Placement.
items.abstract: Chest tube drainage restores negative intrathoracic pressure, which might alter cardiac loading. Digital thoracic drainage systems continuously record pressure and airflow. We examined device-derived pressure and air-flow trends over 48 hours and echocardiographic changes between 24 and 48 hours. Forty-one chest tube drainage episodes in 39 adult, non-mechanically ventilated patients were studied prospectively. Device records were analysed at 10-minute intervals, providing preset suction level, measured circuit pressure, and air flow. Echocardiography was performed at 24 and 48 hours. Continuous time-series analyses included 29 episodes, 28 of which were evaluable within the predefined 48-hour window. False discovery rate correction was applied to multiple comparisons. The preset suction level remained unchanged during the first 48 hours in 21 of 29 episodes (72%), and the measured circuit pressure was closely related to it at each time point (R 2 = 0.838-0.955). Air leak decreased from a median of 61.6 mL/min at baseline to 2.3 mL/min at 24 hours ( P P = 0.55). After correction, ejection fraction (q = 0.011) and mitral E velocity (q = 0.007) were higher at 48 hours. No device-derived variable was associated with echocardiographic changes after correction for multiple comparisons. Measured circuit pressure appeared to reflect regulated drainage-system pressure more closely than pleural physiology. Most reduction in air leak occurred before the first echocardiographic assessment, potentially limiting the detection of cardiopulmonary associations. These findings support a cautious interpretation of digital drainage parameters and may help define the assessment window for future studies.

items.title: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic clustering capture distinct clinically relevant aspects of carotid atherosclerosis.
items.abstract: Patients with carotid atherosclerosis exhibit substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation, plaque characteristics, and future cardiovascular risk, which do not always align. Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk. We analysed 1075 patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with matched clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data. Unsupervised clustering was applied separately to each data modality, and resulting clusters were evaluated for overlap and association with current symptom status and 3-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Clusters derived from different modalities showed limited overlap, but distinct associations with clinical outcomes. Clinical clusters were most strongly associated with 3-year MACE, whereas histological and transcriptomic clusters were more closely related to current cerebrovascular symptoms. Transcriptomic clusters further delineated molecular pathways and plaque biology. Integration of modalities provided modest improvement in outcome stratification, indicating that these data types capture complementary rather than redundant information. Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data capture distinct but complementary aspects of carotid atherosclerosis, reflecting systemic cardiovascular risk, local plaque phenotype, and underlying biology, with differing relevance to current cerebrovascular symptoms and future cardiovascular risk. The choice of data modality should therefore be guided by the intended clinical or biological question, rather than assuming a single approach can capture the full disease spectrum.

items.title: [Associations of body mass index and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring parameters with left ventricular mass index in children with primary hypertension].
items.abstract: To investigate the associations of body mass index (BMI) and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) parameters with left ventricular mass index (LVMI) in children aged 10-17 years with primary hypertension. A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 151 children aged 10-17 years with primary hypertension admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital from January 2021 to January 2025. Multivariable linear regression was used to analyze the associations of BMI and ABPM parameters with LVMI. Among the 151 children, 115 were boys (76.2%), 109 (72.2%) were obese, and 31 (20.5%) had relatively elevated LVMI (LVMI ≥ the 90th percentile, a threshold not used as a clinical diagnostic criterion for left ventricular hypertrophy); the detection rate of relatively elevated LVMI was higher in the obese group than in the non-obese group (24.8% vs 9.5%, P P P (P >0.05); these associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses using BMI Z-score. In children with primary hypertension, BMI and ABPM diastolic parameters are closely associated with elevated LVMI. Greater attention should be given to weight management and to the value of ABPM diastolic parameters in identifying relatively elevated LVMI. 目的 : 探讨10~17岁原发性高血压患儿体重指数（body mass index, BMI）及动态血压监测（ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, ABPM）参数与左心室质量指数（left ventricular mass index, LVMI）的相关性。 方法 : 回顾性分析2021年1月—2025年1月河北省儿童医院收治的151例10~17岁原发性高血压患儿的临床资料，采用多元线性回归分析BMI、ABPM参数与LVMI的关系。 结果 : 151例原发性高血压患儿中，男性115例（76.2%），肥胖109例（72.2%），LVMI相对升高（LVMI≥ P 90 ，该阈值不作为左心室肥厚临床诊断标准）31例（20.5%）;肥胖组LVMI相对升高检出率高于非肥胖组（24.8% vs 9.5%， P P P P >0.05），上述关联在采用BMI Z值的敏感性分析中保持稳健。 结论 : 原发性高血压儿童BMI及ABPM舒张压参数与LVMI升高密切相关，临床应重视体重管理，并关注ABPM舒张压参数对识别LVMI相对升高的价值。.

items.title: Real-World Use and Clinical Outcomes of Jetstream Atherectomy Extending to the P2/P3 Popliteal Artery Segments: Results of the PULSAR Study.
items.abstract: Endovascular treatment of mid- and distal popliteal artery (P2/P3) lesions remains challenging owing to repetitive mechanical deformation and concerns regarding permanent stent implantation. In this setting, Jetstream atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation; however, data on its use in the P2/P3 segments, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 443 limbs of 381 patients who underwent Jetstream atherectomy for femoropopliteal artery lesions in a multicenter registry. Limbs were classified by the most distal segment treated with Jetstream into the SFA/P1 and P2/P3 groups. The primary outcomes were procedural characteristics and periprocedural safety, including distal embolization (DE). Secondary outcomes were 1-year primary patency (PP) and freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularization (CD-TLR). The Jetstream atherectomy was extended to the P2/P3 segments in 94 limbs (21.2%). Distal protection was more frequently used in the P2/P3 group (90.4% vs. 80.8%, p = 0.035). Overall DE occurred in 37.2% of the P2/P3 group and 33.8% of the SFA/P1 group (p = 0.51), whereas DE requiring endovascular intervention was numerically more frequent in the P2/P3 group (9.6% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.067). Jetstream use extending to the P2/P3 segments was not independently associated with overall DE (adjusted odds ratio 1.22, 95% CI 0.72-2.07; p = 0.47). At 1 year, PP was 84.4% in the P2/P3 group and 85.0% in the SFA/P1 group (p = 0.74), whereas freedom from CD-TLR was 89.9% and 90.8%, respectively (p = 0.50). Jetstream atherectomy extended to the P2/P3 segments in approximately one-fifth of the treated limbs, with more frequent use of distal protection. Although no clear differences in periprocedural complications or 1-year clinical outcomes were observed, careful attention to DE is warranted.

items.title: Glutamine metabolic reprogramming remodels the immunosuppressive microenvironment and modulates immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma (Review).
items.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming, with glutamine addiction emerging as a central hallmark that extends beyond supporting tumor proliferation. This review synthesizes current knowledge on how glutamine metabolic reprogramming remodels the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and modulates immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma. The molecular basis of glutamine addiction is discussed, focusing on the von Hippel‑Lindau/hypoxia‑inducible factor axis, MYC activation and epigenetic regulation. The mechanisms by which glutamine metabolism orchestrates immune evasion are examined, including tumor immune cell competition, impaired effector T‑cell function, expansion of immunosuppressive populations such as regulatory T cells and M2 polarized macrophages, and upregulation of immune checkpoints. Therapeutic strategies targeting glutamine metabolism, from transporter and glutaminase inhibition to dietary restriction, are summarized along with mixed clinical trial outcomes that underscore the need for patient selection. Candidate predictive biomarkers across genetic, metabolic, immune and imaging domains are also reviewed. This review aims to provide an integrated framework for understanding glutamine‑driven immune modulation and to guide future therapeutic development in ccRCC.

items.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in T‑cell exhaustion: Its contribution to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy (Review).
items.abstract: Mitochondria play a pivotal role in the regulation of T‑cell function, particularly in the context of T‑cell exhaustion within the tumor microenvironment. T‑cell exhaustion, characterized by impaired effector functions and the sustained expression of inhibitory receptors, poses a significant barrier to effective antitumor immunity and limits the success of immunotherapies. Emerging evidence indicates that mitochondrial dysfunction is a contributor to the metabolic and functional decline of tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes. The present review critically synthesizes the available mechanistic and translational literature on mitochondrial dysfunction in T‑cell exhaustion, with particular attention paid to mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and the threshold‑dependent duality of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. The evidence is organized not by pathway alone, but by intervention class and level of evidence, so that the strategies with demonstrated clinical traction can be distinguished from those that remain at the proof‑of‑concept stage. Of note, four intervention classes are discussed: Metabolic reprogramming, enhancement of mitochondrial biogenesis, redox‑directed modulation and intercellular mitochondrial transfer, together with mitochondria‑directed pharmacological and nanoscale delivery platforms. Clinical translation is assessed against trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, of which the most advanced evaluate metformin in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Mitochondrial dysfunction is also placed in the context of other established drivers of exhaustion, the limitations of the available evidence are stated, and the specific questions that need to be answered before mitochondrial targeting can be incorporated into immunotherapy regimens are also stated. Rather than claiming that mitochondrial dysfunction is a single dominant constraint, it is argued herein that its therapeutic value lies in being a mechanistically tractable and pharmacologically accessible component of a multifactorial resistance program.

items.title: [Levels of pertussis toxin-immunoglobulin G and their influencing factors in children aged 0-14 years].
items.abstract: To investigate the levels and age distribution of pertussis toxin-immunoglobulin G (PT‑IgG) in children aged 0-14 years and to analyze the effects of vaccination history, residential area, and other factors on PT‑IgG levels. A cross-sectional study was designed, in which 1 247 children who attended Luzhou People's Hospital for vaccination from June 2024 to December 2025 were enrolled. Sociodemographic information and diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis vaccination history were collected. Serum PT‑IgG levels were measured (≥40 IU/mL was defined as positive). PT‑IgG positivity rates and levels were compared among groups stratified by age, sex, vaccination history, and residential area. The age-related trend in the PT‑IgG positivity rate and the factors influencing PT‑IgG levels were analyzed. Among the 1 247 children, 896 were seropositive for PT‑IgG, with an overall positivity rate of 71.85%; the geometric mean concentration (GMC) was 68.37 IU/mL (95% CI : 64.12-72.89). The PT‑IgG positivity rate showed a downward trend with increasing age ( P 2-7 years, and 62.5% (GMC 45.29 IU/mL) in those aged >7-14 years. The positivity rate was higher in children with complete vaccination (≥4 doses) [78.1% (GMC 75.83 IU/mL)] than in those with incomplete vaccination [17.5% (GMC 36.94 IU/mL)] ( P P <0.05). The positivity rate decreased to 53.9% in children ≥ 5 years after the last vaccination. PT‑IgG levels in children decline progressively with age, and school-aged children aged >7-14 years are an immunologically vulnerable population. 目的 : 调查0~14岁儿童百日咳毒素免疫球蛋白G（pertussis toxin‑immunoglobulin G, PT‑IgG）浓度及其年龄分布，分析疫苗接种史、居住区域等因素对PT‑IgG浓度的影响。 方法 : 采用横断面研究设计，纳入2024年6月—2025年12月在泸州市人民医院进行预防接种的1 247例儿童，收集社会人口学信息及百白破疫苗接种史，检测血清PT‑IgG浓度（≥40 IU/mL为阳性），比较不同年龄、性别、疫苗接种史及居住区域组间的PT‑IgG阳性率和浓度差异，并分析PT‑IgG阳性率随年龄变化的趋势及其浓度的影响因素。 结果 : 1 247例儿童中，血清PT‑IgG阳性896例，总体阳性率为71.85%;PT‑IgG几何平均浓度（geometric mean concentration, GMC）为68.37 IU/mL（95% CI :64.12~72.89）。PT‑IgG阳性率随年龄增长呈下降趋势（ P 2~7岁组为75.9%（GMC 72.18 IU/mL），>7~14岁组为62.5%（GMC 45.29 IU/mL）。完整接种（≥4剂）者阳性率为78.1%（GMC 75.83 IU/mL），高于未完整接种者（17.5%，GMC 36.94 IU/mL）（ P P 结论 : 儿童PT‑IgG浓度随年龄增长逐步下降，>7~14岁学龄儿童为免疫薄弱群体。.

items.title: Cervical cancer risk reduction in the era of human papillomavirus vaccination.
items.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination status is important to consider when evaluating the population-level impact of cervical screening uptake on cervical cancer risk, yet screening rates are rarely presented by vaccination status, limiting assessments of population-level protection against cervical cancer. Using females 21-39 years old from the 2019 National Health Interview Survey (N = 4000), the authors report the proportion up-to-date with cervical screening stratified by age and self-reported HPV vaccination status. Using assumptions of 85% and 70% reduction in cervical cancer risk from HPV vaccination and up-to-date screening status, respectively, the authors explore the population-level reduction in cervical cancer risk from varying screening coverage by HPV vaccination status. A total of 78.4% of females were up-to-date with screening, 38.0% reported ever receiving an HPV vaccine, and 15.3% were both unvaccinated and not up-to-date with screening. Across age groups, the proportion of females up-to-date with screening was 6.3%-19.1% higher for vaccinated versus unvaccinated females. The relative reduction in cervical cancer risk from vaccination and screening ranged from 62.1% for females 36-39 years old to 73.1% for females 26-30 years old, compared to the absence of vaccination and screening. Despite females 21-25 years old having the lowest screening uptake, their reduction in cervical cancer risk was not the lowest due to higher vaccination levels. Cervical screening rates are higher among females who were vaccinated against HPV, resulting in a higher population-level risk of cervical cancer than expected from considering vaccination and screening rates independently. Including vaccination status in national surveillance data sets would help identify and target interventions within communities at higher risk.

items.title: [Characteristics of Laboratory Indices in HLH Associated with CAR-T Cell Therapy --Review].
items.abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a rare and life-threatening clinical inflammatory response syndrome that arises in the setting of genetic mutations, infections, inflammatory, or neoplastic diseases. Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy has been widely used in the treatment of a variety of hematologic malignancies. However, it may cause life-threatening inflammatory toxicities, manifested as cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and CAR-T associated HLH. Timely identification is the prerequisite for preventing CAR-T associated HLH. However, CAR-T associated HLH has mostly been reported in case reports, and there is no unified diagnosis and treatment standard yet. This article reviews the characteristics of laboratory indices, hoping to provide reference for the early diagnosis and treatment of CAR-T associated HLH in clinical practice. CAR-T细胞治疗相关HLH的实验室指标特征. 噬血细胞性淋巴组织细胞增多症（HLH）是一种罕见的、危及生命的临床炎症反应综合征，病因包括基因突变、感染、炎症或肿瘤等。嵌合抗原受体T（CAR-T）细胞疗法正广泛应用于多种血液恶性肿瘤的治疗，但治疗中可能引发危及生命的炎症性毒性，表现为细胞因子释放综合征和CAR-T细胞治疗相关的HLH，及时识别是预防CAR-T细胞治疗相关HLH的前提。然而，目前CAR-T细胞治疗相关HLH多见于病例报告，尚无统一的诊疗标准。本文就CAR-T细胞治疗相关HLH的实验室指标特征进行综述，以期能为临床尽早诊断和治疗该病提供参考。.
items.journal: Zhongguo shi yan xue ye xue za zhi

items.title: Preclinical progress in the target validation of viroporins: candidates for potential target therapy.
items.abstract: Numerous viral infections necessitate immediate attention, underscoring the urgent need for effective antiviral drugs that can directly inhibit viral functions or indirectly manipulate host factors. Most direct-acting antiviral drugs target two specific viral components: polymerases (including reverse transcriptases) and proteases. Focusing on this narrow range of targets limits the scope of drug development and favors rapid resistance emergence. Therefore, targeting alternative viral components, such as viroporins, is advantageous. Viroporins constitute a family of small hydrophobic proteins encoded by viruses that oligomerize to form ion channels, thereby playing crucial roles in various stages of the viral infectivity cycle. Despite their functional significance, they have received considerably less attention from the pharmaceutical industry compared to traditional viral targets. This review delves into the significance of viral channels as potential therapeutic targets, surveying recent advancements and the prospects for future breakthroughs. Viroporins from diverse viral families and their potential inhibition by small molecules are discussed, with special emphasis on bacteria-based channel assays that facilitate high-throughput screening of channel blockers. Bacteria-based assays enable rapid discovery and preemptive resistance mapping, while conserved pore architectures raise the prospect of broadspectrum inhibitors. However, clinical translation requires addressing selectivity, toxicity, and pharmacokinetic challenges. Viral infections can be best managed with efficient antiviral drugs. Most antiviral medicines work by blocking just two parts of a virus: protease and polymerase. Because so many drugs attack the same two parts, viruses can change and stop the drugs from working. This is called drug resistance.This review focuses on a different class of viral proteins called viroporins, which have been less encountered by antivirals. Viroporins are virally expressed ion channels in host cells that allow ions to move in and out of cells. This, in turn, helps the sustainability of viral propagation. Discussion of some well-known viroporins exemplifies the mechanism of ion conduction in these channels and emphasizes how their blockade has been useful in stopping viral propagation.The review describes viroporins from many viruses, including flu, hepatitis C, HIV, SARS-CoV-2, chikungunya, dengue, Zika, West Nile, and mpox. Conventional electrophysiology measures the flow of ions directly. However, it is a specialized technique and requires considerable experimental effort. On the other hand, another high-throughput method has been discussed that uses bacteria as a tool to assess viroporin activity. In this method, the bacterial growth rate is directly correlated with channel expression and serves as a reporter of viroporin activity. Moreover, this is useful for identifying channel blockers that could serve as potential antiviral drugs. However, more work is necessary to ensure the effectiveness and safety of these drugs in practice. This review aims to encourage further research into viroporins and accelerate the development of new antiviral treatments.

items.title: A novel role of NOX2 in enhancing HBV replication through ROS‑mediated autophagy activation.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NOX2 affects HBV infection remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the potential role of NOX2 in HBV replication was investigated in cell models. First, it was demonstrated that NOX2 is highly expressed in transiently and stably HBV‑infected cells. Second, by employing inhibitor, RNA interference technique and plasmid overexpression, it was revealed that NOX2 plays an essential role in promoting HBV replication. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of how NOX2 affects HBV replication was illustrated. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication. These results suggested a previously unrecognized role of NOX2 in HBV replication. Taken together, NOX2 may serve as a novel target for developing treatment strategies against HBV‑related disorders.

items.title: Gamma-Glutamyl-Transferase Is Inversely Associated With Mortality in Patients With Cirrhosis and Active Alcohol Consumption.
items.abstract: Gamma-Glutamyl-Transferase (GGT) is a key enzyme in amino acid transport and in glutathione metabolism, making it essential for the counteraction of cellular oxidative stress. Clinically, it has been widely used as a marker for liver dysfunction and alcohol consumption. In the general population, elevated GGT has been associated with adverse outcomes, although this association is relatively unspecific. Therefore, the objective of the study was to reveal the prognostic capabilities of GGT in patients with alcohol consumption. We assessed the outcome of hospitalized patients with acute decompensation in alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis and compared the predictive ability of GGT in patients with active and inactive alcohol consumption. A total of 313 patients with alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis were included in the study, of which 95 patients had active alcohol consumption (aALD) and 218 were classified as inactive (iALD). In the aALD group, GGT-levels correlated negatively with the MELD 3.0, CLIF-C-OF-Score and CLIF-C-AD-Score. Low GGT was also an independent predictor of 14-day, 30-day, 90-day and 1-year mortality, respectively. Intriguingly, high risk patients (GGT   118 U/L, 1.8%). Low GGT might be a greatly underestimated prognostic marker for mortality in cirrhotic patients with ongoing alcohol consumption and could be used as an additional variable for better risk stratification and selection for liver transplantation in these patients. Patients with alcohol‐associated liver cirrhosis who continue to drink alcohol are at particularly high risk of poor outcome. Our study shows that unexpectedly low, rather than high, serum levels of the routine liver‐function blood test Gamma‐Glutamyl‐Transferase (GGT) were associated with a much higher risk of death in these patients. This phenomenon may help to more accurately identify high‐risk patients and improve selection of patients for liver transplantation.

items.title: Pharmacotherapy options for managing hepatitis B in children: an update.
items.abstract: Children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may face decades of infection before developing advanced liver disease. Although antiviral options have expanded, pediatric management remains challenging because of age-dependent treatment eligibility, limited long-term evidence, and uncertainty regarding functional cure. This narrative review examines treatment indications, international guidelines, and the efficacy and safety of interferon-based therapy and nucleos(t)ide analogues in children and adolescents. International guidelines were prioritized, supplemented by PubMed and Cochrane Library searches through September 2026 without a lower publication-date limit. We discuss treatment withdrawal and developmental safety, including management during immunosuppression, considerations for special populations and transition to adult care. Emerging therapies are assessed with particular attention to the limits of applying adult results to children. In our view, earlier treatment deserves studies, but younger age alone is insufficient grounds for intervention. Favorable responses in selected childhood cohorts do not establish that treating all children with high viremia improves lifelong outcomes. Bepirovirsen offers a concrete route toward finite therapy by reducing HBV transcripts, yet adult efficacy cannot establish pediatric benefit. Over the next five years, adolescent trials should determine whether such treatment could achieve sustained HBsAg loss after withdrawal without unacceptable toxicity. Until then, effective NA suppression remains a clinically valuable option, even when cure is not achieved.

items.title: Increased Hepatitis D Testing in Canada Identifies More HDV-Positive Individuals: A Multi-Provincial Analysis, 2022-2024.
items.abstract: CASL/AMMI 2025 guidelines recommend reflex anti-HDV testing for all hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive individuals, replacing risk-based screening, yet Canadian data on HDV testing and detection remain limited. In Canada, only Quebec offers anti-HDV testing; other regions refer samples to the National Microbiology Laboratory (NML), where HDV RNA confirmation is centralised. We assessed HDV testing volume, seroprevalence, RNA positivity, and genotypes in referred samples and randomly selected archived HBsAg-positive samples. Anti-HDV results from Quebec and the NML from August 2022 to July 2024 were analysed and compared with a 2012-2019 national survey. To complement referral-based surveillance, 3386 randomly selected archived HBsAg-positive samples from five provinces were tested. Seropositive samples underwent HDV RNA testing and genotyping at NML. Among 8401 unique referred samples, 271 (3.2%; 95% CI, 2.9-3.6) were anti-HDV positive, of which 117 (43.2%; 95% CI, 37.4-49.1) were HDV RNA positive. Compared with 2012-2019, annual testing volume increased fourfold (1011 to 4201 tests/year), while annual detection increased from 48 to 136 anti-HDV-positive individuals and from 31 to 59 HDV RNA-positive individuals. Among archived samples, 67/3386 (2.0%; 95% CI, 1.6-2.5) were anti-HDV positive, and 14/67 (20.9%; 95% CI, 12.9-32.1) were RNA positive. Genotypes 1, 2, 5, 7, and 8 were detected. Increased HDV testing in Canada was associated with greater detection of anti-HDV-positive and HDV RNA-positive individuals despite lower positivity rates. HDV RNA detection and multiple genotypes in archived HBsAg-positive samples support universal reflex anti-HDV testing, with RNA confirmation, harmonised reporting, and integrated HBV/HDV surveillance. Hepatitis D is a serious infection that occurs only in people with hepatitis B and can be missed when testing is based only on risk factors Increased testing identified a greater absolute number of people with hepatitis D virus. Hepatitis D infection was also found in randomly selected archived hepatitis B‐positive samples, showing that some cases exist outside usual referral pathways Multiple HDV genotypes (1, 2, 5, 7, and 8) were detected across Canada, supporting ongoing testing and molecular surveillance.

items.title: Statement of Retraction: Circular RNA circRNA-0039459 promotes the migration, invasion, and proliferation of liver cancer cells through the adsorption of miR-432.
Anticancer efficacy of nitazoxanide for targeting liver metastasis of uveal melanoma by disrupting the cancer bioenergetic profile.
items.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common intraocular malignancy affecting adults. It originates from melanocytes within the ocular tract mainly in the choroid and to a lesser extent in the iris and ciliary body. The incidence of UM varies according to geographical location and ethnicity. Patient mortality is associated with the development of metastasis to the liver, and despite the limited control of the primary cancer and its major therapeutic dilemmas, metabolic needs of cancer have been revealed as a druggable strategy for the treatment of UM. The present study aimed to investigate the anticancer and antimetastatic effects of nitazoxanide (NTZ) using UM (Mel270 and Mel290) cell lines to assess cell viability, cell cycle, and cellular responses through western blot analysis together with a mouse model established by intrasplenic injection to evaluate liver metastasis and tumor incidence. NTZ uncouples the mitochondria by reducing the membrane potential and oxygen consumption rate in UM cancer cells. NTZ treatment in UM cells was demonstrated to notably inhibit cell growth, proliferation and the colony development in cell culture models. Moreover, NTZ halted the cell cycle at G0‑G1 stage, reducing cell migration of UM cancer cells. Mechanistically, acute treatment of UM cells with NTZ stimulated adenosine monophosphate‑activated serine/threonine protein kinase phosphorylation and downregulated mTOR and the acetyl‑CoA carboxylase signaling pathway. Furthermore, oral treatment of NTZ reduced the hepatic metastasis when UM cells were transplanted intrasplenically in male non‑obese diabetic‑severe combined immunodeficient‑γ mouse model. Overall, the findings of the current study reveal the notable role for mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in UM and highlight NTZ‑targeted mitochondrial function as a new therapeutic area to treat the liver metastasis of human UM.

items.title: From network pharmacology to experimental verification: Angelica sinensis and its key constituent β‑sitosterol exert anti‑liver cancer effects through the p53 signaling pathway.
items.abstract: Liver cancer remains a major cause of cancer mortality and the limited benefit of existing therapies leaves a clear need for new therapeutic agents. Although Angelica sinensis (AS) shows broad antitumor potential, its mechanistic basis against liver cancer remains unclear. The present study revealed that AS reduced the viability, proliferation and migration of the HepG2 human liver cancer cell line. Network pharmacology pointed to several putative targets including insulin, peroxisome proliferator‑activated receptor γ, nuclear factor κB subunit 1, estrogen receptor 1 and albumin. By combining molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation and Cell Counting Kit‑8 cell viability screening, β‑sitosterol (BS) was identified from the candidate compounds of AS for further study, based on its stable interactions with central targets and its strong antiproliferative activity against HepG2 cells in vitro . Mechanistic assays of BS revealed that its anti‑liver cancer effect was mediated through the p53 pathway. BS treatment increased the proportion of apoptotic cells, together with increased expression of the tumor suppressor protein p53 and the pro‑apoptotic proteins Bax and Caspase‑3, and reduced expression of the anti‑apoptotic protein Bcl‑2. Co‑treatment with pifithrin‑α hydrobromide, a p53 inhibitor, partly reduced the proportion of apoptotic cells and partly reversed these changes in protein expression, confirming a p53‑dependent mechanism. The present study clarified the mechanisms by which AS, and its active component BS, suppress the proliferation and migration of liver cancer cells and trigger apoptosis through the modulation of the p53 pathway. These results support AS and BS as promising leads for development of plant‑derived therapies against liver cancer.

items.title: Survival outcomes of microwave ablation versus liver resection for gallbladder-adjacent hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter propensity score overlap-weighted study.
items.abstract: Microwave ablation (MWA) and liver resection (LR) are both established treatment options for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but comparative evidence on survival outcomes and safety for gallbladder-adjacent HCC remains lacking. Between January 2006 and December 2024, 1,242 patients with primary HCC from five tertiary hospitals who underwent MWA or LR as first-line therapy were identified. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints were complications, operative time, hospital stay, and costs. Propensity score overlap weighting balanced baseline characteristics, with propensity score matching as a sensitivity analysis. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, log-rank test, and multivariable Cox regression with subgroup analyses. A total of 254 patients were included, with 66 in the MWA group and 188 in the LR group. After overlap weighting, no significant difference in OS was observed ( p  = 0.315), whereas LR showed significantly better PFS ( p  = 0.048). Multivariable analysis revealed that treatment modality was not an independent predictor of OS ( p  = 0.310) or PFS ( p  = 0.096). Subgroup analysis showed no significant treatment interaction for OS ( p  = 0.193) or PFS ( p  = 0.986). MWA demonstrated comparable complications, with shorter operative time, shorter hospital stay, and lower cost than LR (all p  < 0.001). In conclusion, for gallbladder-adjacent HCC, MWA achieved OS and a safety profile comparable to LR, while offering shorter operative time, shorter hospital stay, and lower cost, suggesting MWA may be an effective and less invasive alternative in selected patients.
